items.item: The manifest bound truncation is measured, not assumed: examples.py asserts the real lower_bound and upper_bound returned by table.inspect.data_files() are exactly 16 bytes, against real values of 43 and 200 bytes, per FACT-CHECK.md claims 1-2.

items.item: The upper bound's increment-the-last-byte construction is asserted directly (upper_bound[:15] matches the truncated prefix, upper_bound[15] is exactly one more than the real byte), not just described.

items.item: The Puffin file's container bytes (magic, blob placement, footer JSON, footer payload size, flags) are built to match the spec's File structure and Footer structure sections exactly, verified by an independent raw-byte parse in step 7 that uses no pyiceberg API, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #2.

at.step: Reveal: a real Puffin file, byte-exact to spec, holding a real sketch

items.item: The statistics file is registered through pyiceberg's real public update_statistics()/set_statistics() API, not a low-level workaround, and this is disclosed as a contrast with this chapter's earlier delete-file and manifest-rewrite topics which needed low-level primitives, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #3.

at.step: Reveal: a real Puffin file, byte-exact to spec, holding a real sketch

items.item: The sketch's own serialized bytes are a disclosed, from-scratch substitute for the real Apache DataSketches library's wire format -- the spec names that exact library, and this repo's baseline environment has no dependency on it, matching this chapter's established sketch-implementation convention (Chapter 5's HyperLogLog topic) of building sketch algorithms from first principles rather than adding new pip dependencies with no install path in this repo's build pipeline, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1.

at.step: Reveal: a real Puffin file, byte-exact to spec, holding a real sketch

items.item: The sketch estimate vs. true distinct count comparison is an exact computed percentage (not eyeballed), consistently near 0.3% across 3 determinism-check runs on 20,000 rows, printed by examples.py itself.
